current_evidence: Not verified: the shared WebFetch budget (400/hour) was exhausted and returned HTTP 403 on 3 attempts, and the WebSearch budget for this turn was used up, so neither the PDF nor the council planning page could be fetched.

issues.detail: List date 2026-08-01 is taken from PDF metadata CreationDate, not an adoption or publication date in the document text. The filename 'lvc-adopted' suggests an adoption date is printed in the document, but Grokbot did not record it.

About 30 local requirements are placed under Full planning only, with the note 'INFERRED: application type not named ... placed under Full planning'. Examples are Biodiversity Survey, Land Contamination, Daylight/Sunlight, Flood Risk Assessment, Heritage Statement, Lighting Assessment and Trees. Meanwhile Householder, Outline, Reserved matters, s73 and Demolition in conservation area are all marked '(none) - national requirements only'. Grokbot's own extracted text shows the list applies to householder work as well.
issues.evidence: tab_items: 'For householder applications the key dimensions are the external width, height and depth of the proposed works'; Householder row: 'No specific local requirements identified'

issues.detail: Biodiversity Net Gain is placed under 'Works to trees'. The excerpt is part of the BNG exemption list (works to trees where no fee is required are exempt), so the placement reverses its meaning.
issues.evidence: Works to trees row: '...area and works to trees, where no fee is required.'

issues.detail: Noise Impact Assessment is placed under Advertisement consent. The excerpt runs the words 'Application for advertisement consent' (from an adjacent table row) into the noise assessment description. Nothing shows that noise assessments apply to advert consents.
issues.evidence: Advertisement consent row: 'Application for advertisement consent A Noise Impact Assessment should include the following information...'

issues.detail: Fire Statement is placed under 'Change of use - prior approval' on the strength of a sentence that describes when a Fire Statement is NOT required. The real trigger (relevant buildings of 18m+ or 7+ storeys, for planning applications) is not given.
issues.evidence: 'Fire Statements are not required where a material change of use of a high rise building, would mean the building was no longer a relevant building.'

issues.detail: Table rows are merged, so requirements carry other rows' triggers. 'Arboricultural Impact Assessment / Tree Survey' and 'Travel Plan' both carry the Travel Plan trigger (significant transport movement). 'Affordable Housing Statement' and 'Self-build' carry the Historic Impact Statement trigger (heritage assets affected). 'Archaeological Assessment' runs into '27 Hot Food Takeaway'. 'Environmental Statement (EIA)' runs into BNG text about a '10% net gain'.
issues.evidence: Arboricultural row: 'Survey and Tree Protection Plan ... Required for applications likely to that generate signiﬁcant amounts of transport movement.'

issues.detail: Several rows have no usable trigger, only an unrelated or cut-off fragment. Schedule of works (listed building): 'an arboricultural method statement.'. Marketing: 'use e.g. marketing information.'. Viability: 'be delivered a viability assessment will be required (see below).'. Sunlight to gardens: 'gardens or amenity space.'. Photographs: soakaway infiltration-test text. Foul Sewage: Housing Statement text. Flood Risk Assessment and Heritage Statement: generic 'must not be a placeholder' boilerplate. Design and Access Statement, Site levels and Roof plan: legislation citations from the national list that cut off mid-sentence.
issues.evidence: Schedule of works row trigger: 'an arboricultural method statement.'

issues.detail: 'Minerals / Waste specific statements (county matters)' is a misclassification. The text is the city's Waste Minimisation Statement for major development (Gloucestershire Waste Core Strategy WCS2), not a county-matter minerals or waste requirement.
issues.evidence: '63 Waste Minimisation Statement JCS SD3 Gloucestershire Waste Core Strategy, Policy WCS2 Major development'

issues.detail: The 'Submission rules' tab items are process text, fees or garbled fragments, not requirements. They include the 28-day invalid-letter return rule, the admin fee for returning applications, URL fragments ('NPPG Air Quality .gov.uk/media/euilev1o/...', 'A guide for small 10 ov.uk/media/k0ppalty/...'), the BHL guidance pdf name, and a run-on list of item names ('- Masterplan - Housing stock conditions survey ... 22 23 Fall Prevention from Taller Buildings Flood Risk Assessment GCP C7'). Drawing-standard items carry stray list numbers ('2.', '3.', '4.', '5.'). The 'Policy-driven requirements' item is a sentence fragment from the HRA trigger.
issues.evidence: tab_items: 'An admin fee will be charged for processing and returning the application.'

issues.detail: The workbook counts only 42 items, but item numbers in the extracted text run to at least 63. Local items named in Grokbot's own text have no requirement row with a proper trigger: Air Quality Assessment, Hot Food Takeaway information (GCP C4), Changing Places Toilet specification, Estate Regeneration checklist, Fall Prevention from Taller Buildings, Building for a Healthy Life assessment, Odour risk assessment for commercial kitchens, Housing Statement (unit numbers and mix), Student Accommodation statement, Foul Drainage Assessment Form FDA1 (non-mains drainage), Waste Minimisation Statement (major), and Noise Impact Assessment for full applications. Exact triggers are not verified against the source.

issues.detail: Listed building consent has only the Design and Access Statement. The Historic Impact / Heritage Statement ('Required for planning applications where heritage assets are affected') is not placed under Listed building consent, Householder or Demolition in conservation area.
issues.evidence: '16 26 Historic Impact Statement NPPF Required for planning applications where heritage assets are affected.'

summary: The live source could not be fetched because the WebFetch and WebSearch budgets were exhausted, so the link and its currency are unverified and the date rests only on PDF metadata. Grokbot's own extraction is badly garbled: merged table rows give requirements the wrong triggers, BNG and Noise are placed under the wrong application types, process and fee text is listed as requirements, Householder is wrongly marked national-only, and roughly a dozen numbered local items are missing.

withdrawn_issues.detail: The CIL Additional Information Form is placed under Lawful development certificate with the trigger 'for 11 to 449 dwellings'. This looks like a threshold merged in from another row. The CIL form normally applies to any proposal creating new dwellings or 100 sq m or more of new floorspace, so this threshold is probably wrong. Needs checking against the source.
withdrawn_issues.evidence: 'CIL Additional Information Requirement Form planning permission/lawful development certiﬁcates for 11 to 449 dwellings.'
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: The threshold is in the source and is not merged in from another row: the CIL row reads "Applications for full planning permission/lawful development certificates for 11 to 449 dwellings" (plus reserved matters for 11 to 449 dwellings).
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. The 11-449 dwellings threshold is in the council's own text.
